extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of Shakespeare; educated general readers interested in literary history
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for studying and judging Shakespeare's life and plays, blending historical/archival methods with literary and dramatic criticism. Includes recommended primary repositories for biographical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/contextual study
rubrics_metrics.description: Study Shakespeare in relation to his time and environment: use knowledge of Elizabethan literature, drama, theater to explain his development and to account for qualities of his achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study aims not merely at appreciation of his work, but to explain development and account for qualities; approach is that of the scientific historian examining records to understand causes, results, and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical dramatic criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Unite knowledge of the Elizabethan theater with interest in drama as a peculiar form, studying Shakespeare as a dramatist rather than merely as a poet or philosopher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine theatrical/technical knowledge with dramatic form concerns to evaluate plays on dramatic, not only poetic, grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of development and chronology
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace the evolution of the drama and determine the chronology of the plays as the basis for assessing Shakespeare's development and achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition of growth of his powers via careful chronology is a necessary basis for a just estimate of the plays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of documentary records and early traditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on documentary records and early traditions (legal and court documents, parish registers, wills, corporate records) as primary authorities about Shakespeare's life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These patient investigations into legal and court documents are almost the only records preserved that can bear on Shakespeare's life; they should be the basis for biographical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious use of the sonnets for biography
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the sonnets as possible sources for the man's nature and emotional conflicts but with caution: at worst they may be literary exercises on conventional themes, at best genuine emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let sonnet-based inferences contradict impressions from the plays; sonnets add little to what the plays already imply about the man.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer personality mainly from the plays
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive conception of Shakespeare the man primarily from the impressions of personality implied by the plays rather than solely from external records or the sonnets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plays reveal characteristics (self-control, industry, emotional range) consistent with documentary traditions; biographical portraits should accord with dramatic impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as chief source of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the plays chiefly by their poetry — the beauty and imagery of language — which, together with characterization, underlies their lasting preeminence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry is adapted to speakers; even when verse becomes undramatic it supplies fancy or melody; readers' pleasure lies in the flow of words endowing persons and moments with color and suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization as chief source of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess Shakespeare by the range, vitality, and psychological penetration of his characters; characterization and poetry are inseparable sources of admiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters are magnificent portraits often transcending stock types; their psychological complexity, even if not strictly consistent, produces penetrating and question-provoking psychology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary and daring linguistic invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Value Shakespeare's enormous and daring treatment of vocabulary — coining, changing, or repurposing words to capture significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An enormous vocabulary is treated with daring freedom so that words are coined or restamped to let nothing of significance escape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery and figures over mere musical line
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider imagery of words themselves (fresh trope, unexpected meaning) as more decisive than mere music of the line for poetic quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of poetry depends less on the music of line or passage than on imagery; sometimes an excess of figures results, but when restrained to character and situation the effect is gorgeous yet ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of poetry to dramatic task
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer poetry that adapts to the dramatic requirements of character and situation, even when sacrificing clarity or harmony to make lines significant of thought and emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As Shakespeare's art matures, the poetry discards verse limitations to serve dramatic task, sometimes sacrificing clarity to convey individual thought and emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken images and richness of suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciate broken rather than completed images and richness of suggestion rather than unity of impressiveness as hallmarks of Shakespearean effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effect is bewildering enchantment through surprise and novelty in words rather than perfected form; the reader enjoys flow and suggestiveness more than final development of each idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of human nature and individualism
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plays by their portrayal of human nature — idealization that grants magnitude and potency to individual souls, making the individual central to imaginative literature's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shakespeare's focus on individual human beings ensures continued relevance so long as the study of human nature remains central; admiration may vary with cultural interest in individual vs. system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional range and sympathetic insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Value the range and intensity of emotional life and the warmth of sympathy and sensitivity to human feeling displayed in the plays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plays' imaginative participation in the height and breadth of human feeling is evidence of an author who united intellectual greatness with extraordinary emotional susceptibility and sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Parish Registers of Stratford-on-Avon
rubrics_metrics.description: The Parish Registers of Stratford-on-Avon are authorities for baptisms and burials of Shakespeare's family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edited registers (Parish Registers Society) provide baptism and burial records (e.g., baptisms of John Shakespeare's children, burials of Hamnet, the poet, and his widow) and are primary documentary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Corporation Records of Stratford-on-Avon
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporation records contain correspondence and civic records relevant to Shakespeare (e.g., Quiney-Sturley correspondence, references to 'Wm. Shackespere' in ward inventories, bill of complaint regarding tithes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these municipal records for local legal/civic matters involving Shakespeare and contextual details about property and affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Public Record Office (London)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Record Office preserves mortgages, property purchases, royal warrants, accounts of the Revels, subsidy rolls, and items showing performances at court and corporate licenses related to Shakespeare and his company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult PRO records for legal documents (purchase of New Place), company patents and warrants, Revels accounts listing performances, subsidy rolls, and chancery suit documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Shakespeare's Birthplace Museum (Stratford)
rubrics_metrics.description: The museum holds conveyances, court rolls, and diaries relevant to property transfers and local disputes involving Shakespeare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the museum's documents (conveyance of estates, extracts from court rolls, diaries) for evidence of property dealings and local events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: The British Museum
rubrics_metrics.description: Houses manuscripts such as Manningham's diary (recording performance of Twelfth Night) and mortgage deeds connected to Shakespeare's Blackfriars property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Ms. diaries and deeds in the Museum for contemporary anecdotal records and transactional documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: The Bodleian Library (Oxford)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains Simon Forman's diary (describing performances of Winter's Tale, Cymbeline, Macbeth) and Accounts of Lord Stanhope with payments for performances and rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these manuscripts for eyewitness performance accounts and treasury/rewards entries documenting plays presented at court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Episcopal Register of the Diocese of Worcester
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains bonds and ecclesiastical records (e.g., the marriage bond for Shakespeare and Anne Hathaway).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search diocesan registers for marriage bonds and other ecclesiastical documents relevant to personal events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Library of the Guildhall (London)
rubrics_metrics.description: Holds indentures and legal conveyance documents related to property in Blackfriars purchased by Shakespeare and associates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Guildhall holdings for sale/indenture papers and corporate property records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository: Principal Probate Registry, Somerset House, London
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains Shakespeare's will and testament, detailing bequests and property dispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the probate registry for the authoritative text of the will and testamentary details; the will is quoted as an essential primary source.
